newsitem.title: INDIA: India announces rules for award of coal mines.
newsitem.headline: India announces rules for award of coal mines.

text.p: The Indian government on Friday formally announced guidelines for offering coal mines to state-owned and private firms for captive consumption only, an official statement said.
The government last month in a sweeping overhaul of its ailing coal industry said it will allow Indian companies to mine coal and lignite for captive consumption and sale.
The guidelines said only coal mines in greenfield regions where basic infrastucture like rail or road links is yet to be developed should be offered to domestic private firms.
Coal mines in regions where the state-owned Coal India Ltd has already invested in development of infrastructure for opening new mines, will not be offered to private sector.
"Blocks already identified for development by Coal India Ltd where adequate funding is on hand or in sight should not be offered," the statement said.
"The parties offered coal blocks in the private sector should be asked to bear full cost of exploration in the blocks," it added.
The award of the coal mines to Indian firms will be made on a competitive bidding basis, the statement said.
